extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in New York City history, comedy fans, culture/history enthusiasts
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and explain notable facts, traditions, and institutional history of the Friars Club, with emphasis on its role in comedy (especially celebrity roasts), membership rules, architecture, and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Friars Club Invented the Comedy Roast
rubrics_metrics.description: The first official roast took place in 1949 (Maurice Chevalier) and the club developed the signature 'no-holds-barred' roast format; motto: 'We only roast the ones we love.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roasts are affectionate, witty, and playfully scathing; historically exclusive events (only male members could attend at first). Examples of roastees and roastmasters (portraits in the George Burns Room) include Whoopi Goldberg & Ted Danson, Richard Pryor & Robin Williams, Kelsey Grammar & David Hyde Pierce. Notable roastees: Milton Berle, Johnny Carson, Jerry Lewis, Billy Crystal, Bruce Willis, Betty White, Quentin Tarantino, Terry Bradshaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roastee Chooses the Roastmaster (procedural tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The roastee gets to pick their roastmaster for the evening of barbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural rule frames the event's tone and line-up; portraits of roastmasters and roastees commemorate that relationship in the clubhouse decor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin as a Response to a Ticket Scam / Formation of Press Agents Association
rubrics_metrics.description: The club began when press agents banded together to stop phony reporters who were taking free tickets and sometimes selling them; they created a blacklist and formed the Press Agents Association which evolved into the Friars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This origin story explains the club's early membership base (press agents) and its ethos of professional solidarity; membership historically included clients (playwrights, actors, comedians, singers, dancers) who occasionally attended meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Time Capsule Buried in the Building
rubrics_metrics.description: A time capsule was buried beneath stone under one of the clubhouse's front windows in 2004 (to be opened in 2104); a 1904 capsule was opened at the club's centennial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1904 capsule contained period news clippings and small items; the 2004 capsule invited each Friar to leave a note, underscoring the club's sense of continuity and ritual around anniversaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clubhouse Architecture Includes Hidden Doors, Closets and Service Passages
rubrics_metrics.description: The clubhouse, originally a 1909 five-story English Renaissance Tudor residence, retains original architectural features including hidden doorways in hallways that lead to a service stairwell with a dumbwaiter, swinging walls revealing small hidden cabinets behind a pool-cue rack, and walls that open to reveal hidden closet space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These features were part of the original home (not added by the Friars) and have been repurposed: residential spaces became dining rooms, bars, event spaces; the former carriage house is now the Frank Sinatra Dining Room; a sixth floor is administrative and the fifth floor houses a gym and sauna.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Clubhouse is Supposedly Haunted
rubrics_metrics.description: Members and staff have reported paranormal activity—shadows and sounds (like shuffling feet) particularly in the George Burns Room; the clubhouse was featured on Ghost Hunters (Season 7, episode 18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legend attributes at least one spirit to comedian Al Kelly, who died at the clubhouse in 1966 after performing at a roast; such stories are part of the clubhouse lore and public mythology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liza Minnelli Was the First Female Friar (membership gender rules history)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Friars Club was male-only from its founding in 1904 until Liza Minnelli became the first female Friar in April 1987.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before women were admitted as members they were barred before 4:00pm and could only visit as dinner guests; women were rarely roasted (Lucille Ball in 1961 was among the few), Joy Behar was the first female Roastmaster in 1997; the club now lists many illustrious female members (Barbra Streisand, Whoopi Goldberg, Carol Burnett, Betty White, Sarah Silverman, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Friars Club Has Been Used as a Filming Location
rubrics_metrics.description: The clubhouse has served as a backdrop for films and TV (e.g., The Comedian with Robert De Niro) and series such as The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel (scenes in the grand foyer and a roast scene).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The club's rooms (e.g., Barbra Streisand Room) are visually notable and have hosted related industry events (after-parties), underlining the clubhouse's cultural visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Friars Club Engages in Philanthropy
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond roasts and awards, the club runs philanthropic programs: The Lincoln Awards (honors service to veterans/military families), The Sunshine Committee (entertainment/companionship for seniors and disadvantaged children), and Adopt-A-Scholar (four-year scholarships for performing-arts students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Friars Foundation accepts donations 'for the betterment of society through the arts'; the club regularly hosts benefits supporting varied causes, showing institutional civic engagement beyond entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Is Becoming More Inclusive (broadened definition of 'entertainer')
rubrics_metrics.description: While early members were largely press agents and composers, and later comedians, the club has in recent years opened membership to non-traditional entertainers such as food personalities, reality stars, and social-media influencers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shift reflects changing definitions of entertainment and the club's adaptation to contemporary media landscapes; it signals both diversification of membership and evolving social relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Head of the Club Is Called the Abbot (ceremonial title)
rubrics_metrics.description: The clubhouse is called the Jerry Lewis Monastery and its ceremonial head is titled the Abbot; notable Abbots have included Frank Sinatra, Milton Berle, Ed Sullivan, Jerry Lewis, and Larry King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title is ceremonial with no religious affiliation, reinforcing the club's monastic-themed traditions and pageantry.
